findings.title: Known native CPU-endpoint/delivery failure does not close the owner admission gate
findings.trigger: The real borrowed observer RLIMIT_CPU soft6 endpoint occurs after successful pidfd publication. Native pidfd_send_signal fails (for example EPERM in a controlled syscall-failure negative); the second attempt at restore_parent also fails. The original wall deadline has not expired.
trace: bound_signal sets cpu_hit and signal_errno but does not make the eventual positive clone result an error.

frw_spawn stores root_pid, sets error=0 for successful clone, retries delivery at restore_parent, then returns root_pid whenever rollback_errno is zero. Neither cpu_hit nor signal_errno changes that return.

NativeBirth.spawn accepts the positive PID. The caller waits for exec and binds the child. Its sole pre-gate test is wall.expired / monotonic deadline; frw_expired does not include cpu_hit or signal_errno.
The caller can therefore write B and release the still-live owner to execute its finite sequence. signal_error is inspected only in finish_observation after custody.finish.
findings.impact: The eventual receipt cannot be a successful package because signal_error is recorded, so this is not a false PASS allegation. It is an avoidable continuation of candidate work after the source has observed its own CPU endpoint and failed the requested termination. Closing the unreleased gate would already force the existing owner entry to fail rather than start modes. This violates the stated abort/terminate behavior and stop-on-loss-of-control boundary.
findings.bounded_fix_requirement: Latch and propagate a CPU endpoint or native delivery error into the caller failure path before releasing the gate, while preserving the exact born PID/pidfd for cleanup. Do not replace the original clock, retry birth, or discard the failed-delivery evidence.
findings.verification_required: On final repaired bytes, qualify genuine post-publication soft6 crossing plus controlled delivery failure; observe zero gate release/new mode admission, persistent exact custody, and terminal accounting or explicit STOP_UNCONFIRMED. Original180/6/45 and other controls remain unchanged.
findings.scope_limit: This uses the implemented source-created CPU endpoint and its own errno path, not arbitrary observer death, hostile stop, or a new supervisor requirement. Original-deadline SIGALRM has a pre-gate expired check and is not claimed to share this particular gap.

findings.title: Native PID recovery and final wait4 are skipped when kill_root raises first
findings.trigger: A root was born but the Python spawn call raises before proc/custody assignment, as already covered by the prepared pending-Python-exception or native-restoration-failure controls. The following kill_root also raises on a delivery error.
trace: Native state has already stored root_pid and owns the birth pidfd before AfterFork_Parent / return.
The caller exception handler executes wall.kill_root before reading wall.pid or creating the retained Custody object, all in one try block.
A kill exception jumps directly to native_custody_error. proc and custody stay None, so neither custody.finish nor the finite final harvest runs.

finish_observation reports no root row; close_after_observation subsequently refuses terminal closure because wall.pid remains set. The source reports failure honestly, but abandons an available exact wait handle rather than attempting the existing permitted reap path.
findings.impact: A signal syscall failure does not imply that the PID accessor or wait4 is unavailable. For example a child can terminate from the still-closed gate or its existing bound, yet the caller never attempts its exact wait4. This loses attainable root birth-through-exit usage and closure evidence and contradicts the claimed recovery of native handles on Python exceptions.
findings.bounded_fix_requirement: Recover and retain root PID/custody independently of signal delivery, then record delivery failures separately and run the existing bounded closure/harvest path. Preserve UNKNOWN when evidence genuinely cannot be obtained; never invent zero or repeat the birth/wait/charge.
findings.verification_required: Combine the existing lost-Python-return/restoration negative with a kill failure while leaving exact wait available; require retained root handle, attempted bounded wait/harvest and saved actual usage. Keep a genuine failed-reap path explicitly STOP_UNCONFIRMED.

findings.cause: Relocated execution/launch pin maps retain old hashes for changed effect-admission-proposal and launch-pins. Qualification input map correctly pins current maps, so their own stale nested references remain a real producer-consumer inconsistency. Author static60 checks did not cover all76 internal references.
findings.required_fix: In joined successor rebuild internal pin dependency maps from actual final bytes in dependency order; verify every nested internal map plus retained external-map equality. Do not overwrite old artifacts or weaken hash guards; no execution to rediscover this known mismatch.
findings.observed: 3 mismatches in 76 internal entries, before candidate effects.
